sentences.text: Germany's distinctive role in the Allied Industrial Base is as its integrated equipment maker.
It holds a role in all ten strategic compacts and a core seat in seven, and 93 economies count it as their best-placed trusted partner somewhere in the chain.
Allies rely on it as their largest holder of vehicle supply and, on mixed trade codes, of drivetrain, grid-equipment and wind-part supply.
Its exposure lies in imported fuel, minerals it does not mine, refined rare earths and battery cells, where China supplies 57% of cell and pack imports.
Its industrial effort should keep EV making, drivetrains and grid equipment at the frontier, and catch up in battery cells and components, where its own need is high.
For minerals it should depend deliberately on trusted producers, and development cooperation can add drivetrain and battery capacity with developing partners.
At home, storage, EVs and solar need to be deployed faster.
The high fence belongs around fuel supply, the rare-earth chain, battery control software and transformer steel.
The supply of gas, oil and coal, which takes one to three years to rebuild.
The rare-earth chain from separation to magnets, where China holds 94% of world supply of rare-earth and battery-metal refining and trusted suppliers only 4%.
The control software of imported battery systems, and grain-oriented electrical steel.
The answer is trusted contracts, stocks and control of command paths, not self-sufficiency.
Keep EV and charger manufacturing, EV drivetrain components and transformers and switchgear at the frontier, with support tied to benchmarks.
Catch Up in battery cells and packs and battery components.
Battery materials refining serves allies more than German need.
Reactor supply is an allied commitment, not a national build; its trade codes mix in boiler parts.
Battery and EV minerals from trusted producers such as Australia, Canada and the United States, where allied supply covers the need.
With developing partners, add trusted battery capacity through development finance, guarantees and offtake; drivetrain rests on German need alone and its Preserve design sets no partner finance.
Accelerate battery storage, EV adoption and solar power, buying commodity hardware competitively from trusted suppliers, with security conditions on connected equipment.
Leave open wafers and PV cells, grid components and coal-plant equipment.
In Figure 1, the first column holds the fuels and minerals Germany imports, and the components and assembly columns its industrial core.
Orange corner flags mark High-fence parts inside other steps: battery software, rare-earth magnets and electrical steel.
Violet flags mark Catch Up layers inside Watch steps, such as solar-grade polysilicon.
Each cell is a supply-chain step of a technology, colored by its strategic choice.
A corner flag marks a mixed step whose named parts sit behind a different fence: in battery cells and packs, the battery software is Secure, the cells Catch Up and the enclosures Watch.
A dotted outline marks a review case, a call resting on low confidence, a review flag, a thin anchor or a known data artifact.

Each technology is split into supply-chain stages from extraction to recycling, and each step gets a strategic choice by fixed rules applied in order:
Secure where an acute vulnerability is measured;
at deployment, Accelerate where deployment need reaches 60;
Watch where the step is a large, commoditized yard;
Preserve where Competitive Position is in the top quarter (75) and either Strategic Industrial Value (bar 60) or supply-chain need (bar 67) is high;
Catch Up where the value is high, the position is not, and a capability anchor is corroborated by other evidence;
Partner where supply-chain need is high but there is neither a top-quarter position nor, for a high-value step, a credible pathway;
Named layers inside a step, such as control software or magnets, take their own choice, and a step whose parts sit behind different fences is mixed.
A value that rests on market size alone is capped just under the bar.
Observed policy never decides a choice.

The high fence (Secure) protects what cannot be allowed to fail; the medium fence covers capabilities worth building, keeping or sourcing deliberately and deployment to accelerate; the low fence (Watch) leaves a step open to competitive purchase.
